single.text:
ASSESSMENT OVERVIEW: The proposal claims $30,000/month in savings, totaling $360,000 annually. Costs include two nurses at $95,000 each ($190,000 total) plus a $15,000 referral bonus, resulting in total Year-1 costs of $205,000. Subtracting costs from savings yields a net Year-1 saving of $155,000. This figure exceeds the user's minimum constraint of $100,000. All stated constraints are satisfied. Key facts: Annual savings: $360,000; Total Year-1 costs: $205,000; Net Year-1 savings: $155,000.
POINTS OF NOTE: No concrete constraint violations flagged.
SUGGESTED NEXT STEP: None required; stated constraints appear satisfied.

raw.overview: All three advisors unanimously recommend proceeding with the hospital float-pool hiring plan, as each confirms the proposal satisfies the critical constraint requiring Year-1 net budget savings of at least $100,000. Each assessment verifies that projected savings from eliminating emergency overtime exceed $300,000 annually while accounting for new staffing costs and associated fees, resulting in net savings well above the threshold.
raw.points_of_note: While Advisor 1 calculates net savings at $170,000 (using $190,000 in new costs), Advisor 2 reports $250,000 net savings (using $110,000 total costs), and Advisor 3 determines $155,000 net savings (using $205,000 total costs). These variations stem from differing interpretations of cost components—specifically whether the $15,000 item represents a one-time referral bonus versus recurring annual expense—and how expense categories are aggregated, though all figures satisfy the $100,000 minimum requirement without violating any stated constraint.
raw.suggested_next_step: Proceed with approval of the hospital float-pool hiring plan, as all advisor assessments confirm the Year-1 net savings exceed the $100,000 threshold and no constraint breaches were identified.
